_comment: PLC Guardian config. Edited live during the demo: the proxy re-reads this file when it changes. Values marked [UNVERIFIED] are placeholders until the PLC register map exists.

192.168.8.2.name: HMI (team laptop running updated HMI project, seen in Test1 2026-10-21)

unknown_sources._comment: Anything not in authorized_sources. allow_reads=false blocks even reads from unknown hosts.

protected_points.name: %M4 Maintenance bypass (ON defeats the level-80 stop)
%MW0 Tank level (= counter %C0.V, computed by the PLC)

%M7 PLCGUARD (D-007 active-response lockout coil; allowed value is 1 while a lockout is in force -- an authorized host writing it back to 0 clears the lockout and must ALERT, not log as a plain AUTHORIZED_CHANGE; added A-030 2026-11-04)

enforcement._comment: mode: 'monitor' = forward everything, detect + log only (demo Iteration 1). 'block' = drop unauthorized requests (Iteration 2). block_response: 'exception' (send Modbus exception) or 'reset' (close the TCP connection).

proxy._comment: Inline mode. Clients connect to listen_host:listen_port; allowed requests are forwarded to upstream (the real PLC). See README 'Inline topology'.

http_gate._comment: D-008: connection-level inline gate in front of the HMI's web API (partial mitigation for RAID R-004 -- see guardian/plcguard/httpgate.py's module docstring for exactly what it does and doesn't cover). Run with 'guardian.py httpgate'; reuses authorized_sources as a per-source-IP allow/deny with no HTTP parsing. Same A-004-style inline-topology dependency as 'proxy' above, not yet built for this leg -- point a test client straight at listen_port to exercise it until then.

http_watch._comment: D-009: passive HTTP-connection trigger for the D-007 lockout, for deployments where Guardian sees the HMI's web traffic on a mirror port but is NOT inline on that segment (no httpgate.py in the path) -- see guardian/plcguard/http_watch.py's module docstring. Off by default; enabling it adds a second trigger source feeding the SAME ActiveResponder instance cmd_monitor already builds for Modbus (shared cooldown), it does not change any Modbus-side behaviour. Enabled 2026-11-09: needs the switch to also mirror the HMI's port (X-003) and a monitor restart to take effect -- cmd_monitor reads this flag once at startup, it is not hot-reloaded the way http_gate.py's config is.

active_response._comment: D-007 reactive PLC-side interlock, monitor mode only. A-027/A-028/A-030 done (S-006): coil 7 = %M7/PLCGUARD, confirmed live over Modbus; active_response.py reviewed PASS (round 2). Re-ENABLED 2026-11-04 after I-009 (first live test false-fired on .2's unlisted FC90 sub-codes; .2's fc90_read_subcodes now complete, re-verified against PM3 + two real captures with zero false positives, A-032). own_ip confirmed as 192.168.8.50. trigger_decisions lists the policy decisions (see policy.py) that fire it; cooldown_seconds limits how often Guardian will re-fire during a burst of attacker traffic. unit 255 matches every other confirmed-working read/write in this project (06_REFERENCE); the PLC also answers unit 1 but 255 is what's actually been exercised.

_comment_map: Register map from the 'Wireshark tank values PLC' chat / plc-guardian-open-items.md section 2. %MW1 meaning unknown, not protected yet.
